stories.title: Model price war: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol and Luna released, prices cut 40-50%
stories.rationale: Major frontier model releases with concrete pricing/capability changes, core reader interest.
stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI followed with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna priced at roughly half their predecessors, triggering industry-wide price cuts of 40-50%. Practitioner analysis notes Luna's strong price-performance for application building, with library and plugin support updated to match.

stories.title: Agentic coding reshapes the SDLC as RoR creator moves to agent-generated code
stories.rationale: Directly targets agentic dev tooling and SDLC automation with concrete practitioner accounts.
stories.summary: 37signals' Ruby on Rails creator says agents now generate nearly all its code, reigniting the 'death of coding by hand' debate, while practitioners caution that agents raise required discipline and can flood teams with unread output. Related coverage examines Windows becoming agent-friendly and design-engineering practices in an agent era.

stories.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
stories.rationale: Concrete capabilities research from a primary lab source in science domain.
stories.summary: Anthropic reports that Claude identified a novel enzyme system exhibiting CRISPR-like repeats. The announcement positions the model as a tool for genuine scientific discovery rather than retrieval.

stories.title: Open-weights momentum: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro trained for $3M tops open leaderboards
stories.rationale: Cheap-to-train frontier open model plus ecosystem tooling; strong signal on open-model economics.
stories.summary: Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro 1T-A42B reportedly became the top open-weights model despite a $3M training cost, while Hugging Face shipped tokenizers v1, llama.cpp quant support in Transformers, and accelerated vision-language models. Together these mark continued cost and accessibility gains in the open ecosystem.

stories.title: TypeSafe AI's Jev introduces 'decision models' returning structured confidence scores
stories.rationale: Novel model architecture directly relevant to agent harnesses and evals; concrete technical detail.
stories.summary: TypeSafe AI unveiled Jev, a 'System One' or decision model that returns floating-point category and confidence scores instead of text, aimed at production decision-making. Independent work has since shown similar single-forward-pass behavior can be approximated from standard LLMs like GLM-5.3-Flash.

stories.title: Stripe acquires OpenRouter for $7B
stories.rationale: Major AI-infra/business acquisition of a widely-used model routing layer.
stories.summary: A Latent.Space discussion reports that Stripe acquired OpenRouter, the model-routing marketplace, for $7B. The conversation covers OpenRouter's path from seed to acquisition amid a proliferation of frontier labs.

stories.title: Google DeepMind ships Gemini 3.8 Live, Live Avatar, and text-to-speech models
stories.rationale: Major model family update with new TTS models and 2,000+ voices, but partly consumer-facing.
stories.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar and two new text-to-speech models offering over 2,000 voices plus custom voice cloning from a 30-second sample. Developers have already built bring-your-own-key playgrounds against the new TTS API.

stories.title: Open-model balance of power, RSI skepticism, and US superintelligence strategy
stories.rationale: Substantive analysis of US-China model gap and policy, aligned with infra/policy interests.
stories.summary: Interconnects published Congressional testimony on the current balance of power in open models alongside arguments questioning true recursive self-improvement, while Import AI covers a US superintelligence strategy. The pieces weigh frontier trajectory and international competition.

stories.title: AI evaluation and safety-standards efforts: reproducible benchmarks and third-party assessments
stories.rationale: Evals-focused, relevant to reader, but heavier on governance than concrete numbers.
stories.summary: UK AISI and EvalEval detailed work to make benchmark results reproducible, while OpenAI outlined principles for third-party safety assessments, global AI standards, a math advisory group, and a new MentalHealthBench. Together they push toward more rigorous, comparable AI evaluation.

stories.title: NVIDIA Warp and MjWarp accelerate robotics simulation workflows
stories.rationale: Concrete compute/robotics tooling from NVIDIA, moderately relevant to infra interests.
stories.summary: A Hugging Face post explains using NVIDIA Warp and MjWarp to speed up robotics simulation and learning workflows. It targets developers building GPU-accelerated physics and RL pipelines.
